api.auth.what_it_is: Server-side Supabase Auth session bridge and one-owner guard. It accepts a token already issued by Supabase Auth; it does not receive or store passwords.
api.auth.can_do:
- `POST /api/auth/session.create`: verifies the access token with Supabase Auth, requires exact configured `OWNER_EMAIL`, then sets a Secure, HttpOnly, SameSite=Lax cookie.
- `GET /api/auth/session.get`: validates the owner cookie, refreshes an expired session when a refresh token is present, and rotates the cookie.
- `POST /api/auth/session.delete`: revokes the remote session when possible and always clears the local cookie.
- Rejects invalid/non-owner identities, cross-origin session creation, malformed/oversized body and incomplete configuration; tokens never appear in JSON responses or logs.
api.auth.limits:
- Password login, signup UI, password reset, OAuth UI and password storage are intentionally not implemented. Supabase Auth owns credential handling.
- Signup remains enabled by Amit's accepted decision; `OWNER_EMAIL` still restricts JARVIS API access to one owner identity.
- Session cookies require HTTPS because they are Secure. There is no separate server-side session table.

api.system.what_it_is: Server-side system endpoints for owner/device identity, kill-switch control and durable event intake/history.
api.system.can_do:
- `GET /api/system/kill.get` returns the current state to the owner or a paired device. Missing/unreadable/malformed state returns 503 with all actions treated as blocked.
- `POST /api/system/kill.set` writes state and an activity audit atomically via `set_system_kill`; a device can only set `kill=true`, owner alone can set false.
- Auth accepts the owner HttpOnly session or a paired device Bearer token; device token is pepper-hashed and looked up server-side. Service-role credentials never go to app/phone.
- `POST /api/system/events.emit` validates registered event schemas, requires `idempotency_key`, forces device source on server, checks a database-backed 60/minute owner limit, and persists duplicates idempotently.
- `POST /api/system/events.list` is owner-only and returns bounded, filtered event history.
api.system.limits:
- It does not execute phone commands or turn the kill switch OFF from a device.
- Migration `0005_event_rate_limits.sql` is a new local migration draft and must be applied by Antigravity to the real project before event intake/rate limiting and atomic kill audit work in production.
- The events table remains outside Realtime publication; `realtime=true` is only metadata for event classification. Realtime stays on `phone_commands`, `system_state`, `tasks`, `reminders`.
- Android secure token storage and native kill UI remain the Android squad's client-side responsibility.

packages.brain.what_it_is: S22 policy for how JARVIS thinks and uses powers. It decides; it does not execute. Enforcement = harness/permissions. Kill switch + audit = safety/.
packages.brain.can_do:
- levels.ts: L0-L4 only. (L0 observe, L1 suggest, L2 act after confirm, L3 act then tell, L4 silent safe+reversible)
- power-registry.ts: validates powers (same rules as DB: id pattern, current<=max, dangerous<=L2, L4 only reversible). newPlugPower() makes a safe new power starting at L0.
- gate.ts: the one gate. Kill ON/unreadable => deny. Unknown power => deny. Otherwise returns mode (observe/suggest/ask_confirm/act_then_tell/act_silent).
- depth-router.ts: FAST / NORMAL / DEEP by rules (no model call), with tunable budgets.
- confirm-wording.ts: wording per level; voice yes only "हाँ / कर दो / भेज दो"; silence never yes; money/health/password confirm by phone voice; money/health/password/vault = voice yes, then owner fingerprint.
- owner-credential.ts: owner fingerprint policy (enrol once in owner login, never deleted, extra ones need owner verify).
- loop.ts: the standard loop with ports; web/screen/message text is data and never starts an action; kill re-checked just before acting.

- `createGateway({...}).call(request)` -> `{ok:true,text,usage,warning?}` या `{ok:false,code,message}`। Codes: `kill_switch_on`, `unknown_model`, `unknown_provider`, `unpriced_model`, `budget_exceeded`, `no_key`, `provider_error`, `timeout`। (built)
- खर्चे की सीमा (`Budget`): रोज़ की और महीने की (भारत की आधी रात से), हर model की रोज़ की सीमा, और free models की रोज़ के requests की सीमा। Call से पहले "सबसे बुरा खर्चा" (अनुमानित input + पूरा output) जोड़कर देखा जाता है, इसलिए सीमा पार करने वाली call होती ही नहीं। 80% पर चेतावनी। (built)
- बिना कीमत वाला (non-free) model मना: कीमत हम अंदाज़े से नहीं भरते। (built)
- Keys: `envKeys()` env से पढ़ता है (`ANTHROPIC_API_KEY`, `OPENAI_API_KEY`, `GEMINI_API_KEY`, नाम `.env.example` वाले)। Key न हो तो बताता है कौन सा variable भरना है, कीमत कभी नहीं। (built)
- Usage: `model_usage` table में हर call (असफल भी, ok=false) दर्ज; `supabaseUsageStore` (service_role, इस महीने की अधिकतम 5000 पंक्तियाँ पढ़ता है) और `memoryUsageStore` (tests)। (built)
- Timeout (default 60 s), और logs में prompt, जवाब या key कभी नहीं। (built)
packages.model-gateway.limits:
- असली providers (Anthropic/OpenAI/Gemini के adapters) अभी नहीं हैं; `Provider` interface है, adapters S13/S07 लिखेंगे। Tests नकली provider से हैं।
- कीमतें और सीमाएँ (`ModelSpec`, `Budget`) कहीं से भरी नहीं गई हैं। इन्हें Amit/S13 settings में तय करें; कीमत देखने की ज़िम्मेदारी भरने वाले की है।
